findings: The primary repository source preserves array + window-size-K -> maximum for every window; the second consolidated source only repeats the problem title. Exact method signature, invalid-k behavior, null behavior and complexity requirement are not preserved source facts.
The candidate explicitly labels null and invalid-k behavior as an adopted executable contract rather than source wording.
The deque stores indices, expires indices at <= i-k, removes dominated tail candidates and exposes the current maximum at the head.
Java extracted directly from the candidate compiles and matches a reviewer-owned quadratic oracle on fixed duplicate/boundary cases plus 3000 deterministic randomized arrays.
Each index is inserted once and removed at most once, supporting O(n) amortized time; at most k live candidate indices support O(k) auxiliary space.
No fabricated production experience or unsupported source-specific API constraint was found.
